mainTopic: The warning not to touch the שלחן and מנורה after the רגל, which vessels need טבילה, and how the gold-coated wooden שלחן can become טמא.
overview: This amud finishes the משנה. Every vessel in the מקדש had backups, and all of them needed טבילה after the רגל except the two מזבחות. רבי אליעזר says the מזבחות are like the ground, and the חכמים say they are exempt because they are coated. The גמרא brings a ברייתא that also warns against touching the מנורה. Our משנה leaves the מנורה out because only the שלחן has ״תמיד״, and the two sides argue about whether ״נכח השלחן״ gives the מנורה ״תמיד״ too. The גמרא then asks how a wooden table that stays in one place can become טמא at all. It answers with ריש לקיש: the שלחן was lifted to show the pilgrims the miracle of the לחם הפנים, which stayed fresh all week. Next the גמרא asks why the gold coating alone does not decide the שלחן's status. Two answers fail according to רבי יוחנן: that acacia wood is too valuable to be cancelled, and that the coating was not fixed. The גמרא begins a new answer, ״the שלחן is different″, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Do not touch the table
steps.stepSummary: The end of the משנה's warning to the עם הארץ: be careful not to touch the שלחן.
steps.simpleTranslation: …that you not touch the table.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of a משנה that started on the previous page. The כהנים warn the עם הארץ not to touch the שלחן of the לחם הפנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The עם הארץ was trusted about טומאה during the רגל, but not once it was over. If he touched the שלחן, it would need טבילה. That would mean taking it out of place, and the לחם הפנים must always be on it.

keyTerms.meaning: The golden table that held the לחם הפנים
A person who is not careful about the laws of purity

phrases.english: that you not touch the table.
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence from the previous page: the כהנים are warning the עם הארץ.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁלֹּא תִּגְּעוּ בַּשֻּׁלְחָן
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The עם הארץ must be warned not to touch the שלחן.

steps.title: Every Temple vessel had backups
steps.stepSummary: Every vessel in the מקדש had a second and third copy, so an impure one could be replaced at once.
steps.simpleTranslation: All the vessels in the מקדש had second and third copies, so that if the first ones became impure, they could bring the second ones in their place.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה tells us that the מקדש kept spare copies of its vessels. That way the עבודה never had to stop because one vessel became impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a practical rule. If a vessel became impure, the backup took its place while the first one went for טבילה.

phrases.english: All the vessels that were in the Temple
had second and third ones,
so that if the first ones became impure —
they could bring the second ones in their place.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל הַכֵּלִים שֶׁהָיוּ בַּמִּקְדָּשׁ יֵשׁ לָהֶם שְׁנִיִּים וּשְׁלִישִׁים
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Temple vessels had backups so that impure ones could be replaced.

steps.title: All vessels need immersion except the two altars
steps.stepSummary: Every vessel needed טבילה after the רגל except מזבח הזהב and מזבח הנחשת. רבי אליעזר says the reason is that they are like the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: All the vessels in the מקדש needed טבילה, except the golden altar and the copper altar, because they are like the ground. These are the words of רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a general rule: after the רגל, all the vessels go to the מקווה. It then names two exceptions, and רבי אליעזר explains why they are exceptions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ground cannot become impure. רבי אליעזר treats the two מזבחות as if they were part of the ground, so they never need טבילה.

phrases.english: All the vessels that were in the Temple
required immersion,
except for the golden altar and the copper altar
because they are like the ground,
these are the words of Rabbi Eliezer,

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל הַכֵּלִים שֶׁהָיוּ בַּמִּקְדָּשׁ טְעוּנִין טְבִילָה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The two מזבחות are exempt from טבילה; according to רבי אליעזר, this is because they are like the ground.

steps.title: The Sages give a different reason: the altars are coated
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים agree that the מזבחות are exempt, but they say the reason is that the altars are coated.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: it is because they are coated.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים agree with the ruling but argue about the reason. They say the מזבחות are exempt because they are coated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree that the two מזבחות do not need טבילה. The argument is only about why. רבי אליעזר says they are like the ground; the חכמים point to the coating.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the חכמים say the מזבחות need טבילה. They agree on the ruling and argue only about the reason.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
because they are coated.
phrases.notes: This is a different reason for the same ruling: the altars still don't need טבילה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהֵן מְצוּפִּין
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the חכמים, the מזבחות are exempt from טבילה because they are coated.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה rules that both מזבחות are exempt from טבילה. רבי אליעזר's reason is that they are like the ground; the חכמים's reason is that they are coated.

steps.title: A ברייתא adds the menorah to the warning
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the warning was: be careful not to touch the שלחן and the מנורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: Be careful lest you touch the table and the menorah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that adds the מנורה to the warning. This sets up the next question: why does our משנה leave the מנורה out?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה mentioned only the שלחן. The ברייתא's version includes the מנורה, so the two sources do not match. That difference is what the גמרא will discuss next.

phrases.english: GEMARA: It was taught:
Be careful lest you touch
the table and the menorah.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: הִזָּהֲרוּ שֶׁמָּא תִּגְּעוּ בַּשּׁוּלְחָן וּבַמְּנוֹרָה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the ברייתא, the warning covers both the שלחן and the מנורה.

steps.title: Why does our משנה leave out the menorah?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the תנא of our משנה did not mention the מנורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And our תנא: what is the reason he did not teach the menorah?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question. Why does our משנה mention only the שלחן and not the מנורה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the ברייתא includes the מנורה, the משנה's silence seems to mean something. The גמרא wants to know the reason behind it.

phrases.english: And our tanna,
what is the reason he did not teach the menorah?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנָּא דִּידַן, מַאי טַעְמָא לָא תָּנֵי מְנוֹרָה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the משנה's warning leaves out the מנורה.

steps.title: ״תמיד״ is written about the table, not the menorah
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says ״תמיד״ (always) about the שלחן but not about the מנורה, so the מנורה can be taken out for טבילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: About the table, ״always″ is written; about the menorah, ״always″ is not written.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that only the שלחן must always stay in its place. So only the שלחן needed the special warning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the מנורה became impure, it could simply be taken away for טבילה and nothing would be lost. The שלחן could not be moved, because the לחם הפנים must be on it ״תמיד״.

phrases.english: About the table, "always" is written,
about the menorah, "always" is not written.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֻׁלְחָן כְּתִיב בֵּיהּ תָּמִיד
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Only the שלחן has ״תמיד״, so only the שלחן must never be removed.

steps.title: The ברייתא: "opposite the table" counts as always
steps.stepSummary: The other תנא says the פסוק ״ואת המנורה נכח השלחן״ ties the מנורה to the שלחן, so it is as if ״תמיד״ were written about the מנורה too.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one: since it is written, ״and the menorah opposite the table,״ it is as if ״always״ were written about it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the ברייתא includes the מנורה. Because the מנורה must stand opposite the שלחן, it shares the שלחן's ״תמיד״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא learns from the placement פסוק that the מנורה must always be across from the שלחן. If so, the מנורה can never be removed either, and it also needed the warning.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one (the other תנא)
It is as if it were written

phrases.english: And the other one:
phrases.notes: This means the תנא of the ברייתא, who did include the מנורה.

phrases.english: since it is written:
"and the menorah opposite the table,"
it is as if "always" were written about it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידָּךְ: כֵּיוָן דִּכְתִיב
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The מנורה is linked to the שלחן by ״נכח״, so it shares the ״תמיד״.

steps.title: The משנה's side: that verse only sets the menorah's place
steps.stepSummary: The משנה's תנא says the ״נכח השלחן״ פסוק only tells us where the מנורה stands. It does not mean the מנורה must always be there.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one: that פסוק comes to set a place for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the משנה's answer to the ברייתא's proof. The פסוק is about location, not about the מנורה always being present.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא read ״נכח השלחן״ as meaning ״always opposite.״ The משנה's תנא reads it only as an address for the מנורה. So the מנורה may still be taken out for טבילה, and the משנה did not need to warn about it.

keyTerms.meaning: That is what it comes for

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה and the ברייתא disagree about the מנורה. The משנה holds that only the שלחן has ״תמיד״. The ברייתא holds that ״נכח השלחן״ gives the מנורה ״תמיד״ too. The משנה's side answers that this פסוק is only about the מנורה's place.

phrases.english: And the other one:
phrases.notes: Now this means the תנא of our משנה, answering back.

phrases.english: that verse is to set a place for it
is what it comes for.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידָּךְ: הָהוּא לִקְבּוֹעַ לָהּ מָקוֹם הוּא דַּאֲתָא
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the ברייתא's reading of ״נכח השלחן״ as meaning ״תמיד״.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק only tells where the מנורה is placed; it says nothing about the מנורה always being there.

steps.title: Why should the table become impure at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that the שלחן can become טמא. It is a wooden vessel made to stay in one place, and such vessels cannot become impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let me learn instead that the table is a wooden vessel made to rest in one place, and any wooden vessel made to rest in one place does not become impure. Why? Because a wooden vessel must be like a sack: just as a sack is carried both full and empty, so too only something carried full and empty can become impure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the whole idea of warning people not to touch the שלחן. Since it is a wooden vessel that stays in one place, it should not be able to become טמא at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה lists wooden vessels right next to a sack when it teaches טומאה. So a wooden vessel only becomes טמא if, like a sack, it gets moved around both full and empty. A large table that stays put fails this test, so why worry about it?

keyTerms.meaning: A wooden vessel made to stay resting in one place
Carried around both when full and when empty
"But let me derive it from...", a way of offering a simpler or different source

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether the שלחן is a real vessel. It is. The question is whether this kind of vessel, one that stays in place, can receive טומאה.

phrases.english: But let me derive it instead
that it is a wooden vessel made to rest in place
and every wooden vessel made to rest in place
does not become impure
What is the reason?
We require it to be similar to a sack
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:32 lists a wooden vessel and a sack together.

phrases.english: Just as a sack is carried full and empty
so too only something carried full and empty can become impure!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתִיפּוֹק לִי דִּכְלִי עֵץ הֶעָשׂוּי לְנַחַת הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the warning about the שלחן (steps 1 and 5) and asks whether the שלחן can become impure at all.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption, shared by the משנה and the ברייתא, that the שלחן can become טמא and so needs a warning
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A wooden vessel that stays in place is not like a sack, so it cannot receive טומאה. The warning seems pointless.

steps.title: The table was carried, as ריש לקיש teaches
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the שלחן was in fact moved around both full and empty. It brings ריש לקיש, who learns from the words 'the pure table' that it can become טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: This table too is carried full and empty, as ריש לקיש taught. For ריש לקיש said: What does the verse mean when it says 'upon the pure table'? By implication, it can become impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the שלחן does count as a vessel that gets carried. It brings ריש לקיש, who shows from a פסוק that the שלחן can become טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the תורה calls it 'the pure table', that implies it could also be impure. So the תורה itself treats the שלחן as able to receive טומאה. The next steps will explain how that fits with the rule from step 10.

keyTerms.meaning: By implication, understood from what the words suggest

phrases.english: This one too
is carried full and empty
as ריש לקיש taught
For ריש לקיש said
What is the meaning of what is written
'upon the pure table'
by implication, it can be impure

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי נָמֵי מִיטַּלְטֵל מָלֵא וְרֵיקָם הוּא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual correction: the שלחן really was carried.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The שלחן always stays in place, so it cannot become טמא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The שלחן was moved full and empty, and the פסוק shows it can become טמא.

steps.title: ריש לקיש asks how the table could be impure
steps.stepSummary: Inside his teaching, ריש לקיש himself asks how the שלחן could become טמא, since it is a wooden vessel made to stay in place.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why? It is a wooden vessel made to rest in place, and such a vessel does not receive impurity!
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש raises the obvious problem with his own reading: a wooden vessel that stays in place should not be able to become טמא. This sets up his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same difficulty as step 10, but now ריש לקיש raises it about the פסוק. He needs to explain how the תורה can call the שלחן 'pure', which implies it could be impure.

phrases.english: And why?
It is a wooden vessel made to rest in place
and it does not receive impurity!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַמַּאי? כְּלִי עֵץ הֶעָשׂוּי לְנַחַת הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: ריש לקיש continues his own statement by challenging it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the שלחן can become טמא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Wooden vessels made to stay in place cannot receive טומאה.

steps.title: They lifted the table to show the pilgrims
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש answers that the כהנים would lift the שלחן with the לחם הפנים on it and show it to the pilgrims. So the שלחן was carried.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the verse teaches that they would lift the table and show the showbread on it to the festival pilgrims. They would tell them: See how beloved you are before God: the bread is as fresh when it is removed as when it was set out.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש explains that the שלחן was actually lifted up on the רגלים to show the people the לחם הפנים. That is why it counts as a carried vessel that can become טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the שלחן was lifted while full of bread, it fits the 'like a sack' test from step 10. The display also showed a miracle: the bread stayed fresh all week, a sign of God's love for the people.

keyTerms.meaning: Pilgrims who come up to ירושלים for the festivals
The showbread, twelve loaves kept on the שלחן
Its removal is like its setting out (it stayed fresh)

steps.whatToRemember: The שלחן can become טמא because it was lifted to show the לחם הפנים to the pilgrims, so it counts as a vessel that gets carried.

phrases.english: Rather, it teaches
that they would lift it up
and show on it to the festival pilgrims
the showbread
and they would say to them
See how beloved you are before God
its removal is like its setting out
phrases.notes: The bread was still as fresh when they took it off as on the day they put it on.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מְלַמֵּד שֶׁמַּגְבִּיהִין אוֹתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers ריש לקיש's own question from step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the שלחן was in fact moved while full, so it fits the 'like a sack' rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The שלחן never moves, so it cannot become טמא.
steps.terutzMaskana: It was lifted with the bread on it, so it counts as carried and can become טמא.

steps.title: The miracle of the showbread
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports the phrase 'its removal is like its setting out' with רבי יהושע בן לוי, who says a great miracle happened with the לחם הפנים, and brings a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רבי יהושע בן לוי said: A great miracle happened with the showbread: as it was when set out, so it was when removed, as it says: 'to place hot bread on the day it was taken away.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the miracle mentioned in step 13. It quotes רבי יהושע בן לוי and a פסוק showing that the bread was still warm on the day it was removed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק calls the bread 'hot' on the day it was taken off the שלחן, a full week after it was baked. That proves the bread miraculously stayed fresh, which is what the כהנים showed the pilgrims.

phrases.english: For רבי יהושע בן לוי said
A great miracle happened with the showbread
as it was when set out, so it was when removed
as it says: 'to place hot bread'
'on the day it was taken away'

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי נֵס גָּדוֹל נַעֲשָׂה בְּלֶחֶם הַפָּנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a source for the miracle mentioned at the end of step 13.
steps.raayaObject: That the לחם הפנים stayed fresh from the day it was set out until it was removed
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהושע בן לוי, based on שמואל א 21:7

steps.title: Why not say the table is impure because of its gold coating?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a simpler reason the שלחן can become טמא: it was coated in gold.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let me derive it instead because of the coating.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why we needed the idea that the שלחן was lifted. We could simply say it becomes טמא because of its gold coating. The next step brings a source for this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A metal vessel can become טמא even if it stays in place. If a vessel's coating decides its status, the gold-covered שלחן would count as metal, and ריש לקיש's explanation would be unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Coating, a covering layer on a vessel

phrases.english: But let me derive it instead because of the coating
phrases.notes: The שלחן was covered in gold, and metal vessels can become impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתִיפּוֹק לִי מִשּׁוּם צִיפּוּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for ריש לקיש's explanation by offering a different reason.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's reason that the שלחן is impure because it was carried
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The gold coating alone should make the שלחן able to receive טומאה, so the lifting explanation is not needed.

steps.title: A משנה shows that a coating decides a vessel's status
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה: a table that broke or was covered in marble can still become טמא only if an uncovered space big enough for cups remains. רבי יהודה says the space must be big enough for pieces of food.
steps.simpleTranslation: For we learned in a משנה: A table or a דולפקי that broke, or that someone covered with marble, and he left on them an uncovered space big enough to set cups, can still become impure. רבי יהודה says: it must be a space big enough to set pieces of food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its question from step 15 with a משנה. The משנה shows that once a wooden table is fully covered with stone, the covering decides its status.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Marble cannot become טמא. The משנה says a covered table can still become טמא only if enough of the wood is left uncovered, so the coating is what counts. By the same logic, the gold-covered שלחן should count as metal. Steps 17–21 try two answers that fail, and step 22 begins a new answer.

keyTerms.meaning: A small table or serving tray
A space big enough to set cups

phrases.english: For we learned in a משנה
a table or a dulpaki that broke
or that someone covered with marble

phrases.aramaic: וְשִׁיֵּיר בָּהֶם מְקוֹם הַנָּחַת כּוֹסוֹת — טָמֵא
phrases.english: and he left on them a space to set cups: it can still become impure
רבי יהודה says
a space to set pieces of food

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּהָתְנַן הַשֻּׁלְחָן וְהַדּוּלְפְּקֵי שֶׁנִּפְחֲתוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source behind the question in step 15.
steps.raayaObject: That a vessel's coating decides whether it can receive טומאה
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in כלים 22:1 about a table covered with marble

steps.title: Maybe acacia wood is too important to be cancelled by a coating
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the שלחן's acacia wood is valuable, so its gold coating does not cancel it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say that acacia wood is different, since it is important and is not cancelled by a coating,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible way out of the question from step 15. Maybe the gold coating does not decide the שלחן's status, because acacia wood is too valuable to be cancelled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה in step 16 showed that a vessel follows its coating, so the gold should decide the שלחן's status. This suggestion says a coating only cancels cheap wood. If that is true, the שלחן is still treated as wood, and ריש לקיש's reason about lifting it is needed after all.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say (introduces a suggested answer)
Acacia wood, the wood of the שלחן
They are cancelled (they lose their own status)

phrases.english: And if you would say:
Acacia wood is different,
since it is important and is not cancelled,
phrases.notes: He means the wood is not cancelled by the gold coating on top of it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: שָׁאנֵי עֲצֵי שִׁטִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a defense against the question in step 15, which was based on the משנה in step 16
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the coating rule to cheap wood
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every coating cancels the wood under it, so the gold decides the שלחן's status
steps.terutzMaskana: Valuable acacia wood stays wood even under gold

steps.title: That works for ריש לקיש but not for רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: The acacia answer fits ריש לקיש, who says expensive wood is not cancelled. It fails for רבי יוחנן, who says even expensive wood is cancelled.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for ריש לקיש, who said the rule applies only to cheap אכסלגים wood from overseas, but expensive מסמים wood is not cancelled. But for רבי יוחנן, who said even מסמים wood is cancelled, what can you say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא checks the acacia answer against an argument between ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן. The answer works for one of them but not the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש holds that only cheap wood is cancelled by a coating, so valuable acacia would not be. רבי יוחנן holds that even expensive wood is cancelled. For him the gold should still decide the שלחן's status, so the question from step 15 comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: This works out well (for one opinion)
A cheap kind of wood brought from overseas
What is there to say? (the answer does not work)

phrases.english: This works out well according to ריש לקיש,
who said: They taught this only
with vessels of אכסלגים wood
that come from overseas,
but vessels of מסמים wood are not cancelled,
so it is fine.
But according to רבי יוחנן, who said:
even vessels of מסמים wood are also cancelled,
what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the acacia answer of step 17 according to רבי יוחנן
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Partial: the answer works only for ריש לקיש
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי יוחנן holds that even expensive wood is cancelled by a coating

steps.title: Maybe the שלחן's coating was not fixed in place
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a second answer: the משנה is about a fixed coating, but the gold on the שלחן was not fixed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say: here, in the משנה, it is a fixed coating, and there, on the שלחן, it is a coating that is not fixed,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second way to say the gold does not decide the שלחן's status. Maybe only a fixed coating cancels the wood, and the שלחן's gold was not fixed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer does not depend on the type of wood, so it could work even for רבי יוחנן. It splits the cases: the coating in the משנה is fixed, while the gold on the שלחן is not, so the gold would not count.

phrases.english: And if you would say:
here it is a fixed coating,
phrases.notes: "Here" is the משנה from step 16 about a covered table.

phrases.english: there it is a coating that is not fixed

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: כָּאן בְּצִיפּוּי עוֹמֵד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 18 left רבי יוחנן without an answer, offers a new distinction
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the cases by type of coating
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The gold on the שלחן counts just like the coating in the משנה
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a fixed coating cancels the wood, and the שלחן's gold was not fixed

steps.title: ריש לקיש already asked רבי יוחנן about kinds of coating
steps.stepSummary: To reject step 19, the גמרא recalls that ריש לקיש asked רבי יוחנן whether the type of coating matters.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't ריש לקיש ask רבי יוחנן: Is this about a fixed coating, or a coating that is not fixed? About a coating that covers the rim, or one that does not cover the rim?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins to reject the fixed-coating answer by quoting a question ריש לקיש asked רבי יוחנן. This step sets up the question, and the next step gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word הא signals that a source is coming that goes against step 19. ריש לקיש asked about two things: whether the coating is fixed, and whether it covers the rim. רבי יוחנן's answer in the next step decides the matter.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't he ask him (introduces a source against the suggestion)

phrases.aramaic: הָא בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מֵרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: But didn't ריש לקיש ask רבי יוחנן:
Is it about a fixed coating,
or about a coating that is not fixed?
About one that covers its rim,
or about one that does not cover its rim?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מֵרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the rejection of step 19 by bringing up an earlier question
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Full rejection of the fixed-coating answer (completed in step 21)
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The type of coating was already asked about directly, and the answer goes against step 19

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the type of coating makes no difference
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that fixed or not fixed, covering the rim or not, the vessel always follows its coating.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he said to him: There is no difference whether it is a fixed coating or a coating that is not fixed, and no difference whether it covers its rim or does not cover its rim.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers ריש לקיש's question: every kind of coating counts. This knocks out the answer from step 19.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If even a coating that is not fixed decides a vessel's status, then the gold on the שלחן must count too. Both suggested answers have now failed according to רבי יוחנן, so the question from step 15 still needs an answer. Step 22 begins a new one.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוחנן, any coating, fixed or not, decides a vessel's status. So the gold coating should have decided the שלחן's status, and both attempts to avoid this failed.

phrases.english: And he said to him:
There is no difference whether it is a fixed coating
or a coating that is not fixed;
there is no difference whether it covers its rim

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא שְׁנָא בְּשֶׁאֵינוֹ חוֹפֶה אֶת לְבִזְבְּזָיו.
phrases.english: or does not cover its rim.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא שְׁנָא בְּצִיפּוּי עוֹמֵד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20, which completes the rejection of step 19
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether only certain kinds of coating decide a vessel's status
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Every kind of coating decides it, whether fixed or not and whether it covers the rim or not

steps.title: A new answer begins: the שלחן is different
steps.stepSummary: Since both attempts failed, the גמרא starts a new answer: the שלחן is a special case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: the שלחן is different —
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the failed answers and opens a new one: the שלחן has its own special rule. This line is a setup, and the explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא means "rather": it throws out what came before and starts fresh. Instead of looking at the wood or the type of coating, the גמרא now says something unique about the שלחן itself decides the matter.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (drops the earlier answers and starts a new one)
The Table in the מקדש that held the לחם הפנים

steps.confusionAlert: Do not stop here thinking the answer is complete. "The שלחן is different" is only the opening, and the reason comes right after.

phrases.english: Rather: the שלחן is different —

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: שָׁאנֵי שֻׁלְחָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After steps 17 to 21 fail to answer the question of step 15, begins a new answer
steps.terutzResolutionType: Special rule for the שלחן (explained in the next part of the text)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The answer must come from the type of wood or the type of coating
steps.terutzMaskana: Something unique about the שלחן itself decides the matter
